newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta scraps crude oil agreement with Libya.
newsitem.headline: Malta scraps crude oil agreement with Libya.

text.p: Malta has scrapped a contract with the National Oil Company of Libya for the supply of crude oil, the Maltese government said on Monday.
But Malta retained a $57.5 million contract for the supply of petroleum products from Libya.

Trade Minister Leo Brincat said in the Maltese parliament that the crude oil contract was not renewed because it was not advantageous for Malta or the state energy corporation Enemalta. Crude will now be bought on the spot market.
Under the agreement with Libya, signed in the mid 1980s and renewed annually, Malta used to buy crude from Libya and Enemalta would bear the cost of refining the crude in nearby Sicily.

A report issued last month on the financial situation at Enemalta said is was not in Malta's interest to renew the agreement and Enemalta would save 1.5 million Maltese pounds (nearly $4 million) by buying refined products from the spot market.
Malta imported 900,000 tonnes of oil in 1996, of which just over half was under the crude oil contract. The cost was was not disclosed.
